what: The official NFL Game Book PDF - the starting-lineup sheet - could not be read in this environment: static.www.nfl.com refuses a TLS handshake from the sandbox and the fetch tool returns 'Failed to fetch page' for every Game Book URL.
why_it_matters: The 'who actually started' side of the availability graph therefore has no value for any fixture. The graph publishes the official Game Book link instead of an inferred starter, and the official NFL inactive list (which the Game Book also carries) is published separately so that a chart name known not to have played is still excluded.
what_would_clear_it: Fetch the 14 Game Book PDFs from a network that can reach static.www.nfl.com and fill the actual-starter column. The inactive half of the gap is already closed by AG-23.

what: Two official game centres (Commanders-Giants and Jaguars-Titans) render both scores as 'Hidden Score' on the read.
why_it_matters: A score cell the official page does not print must not be copied from the page's own hidden field; the final is instead read from the official by-week schedule page, which prints it.
what_would_clear_it: Re-read the game centres after the site restores the score field; the published rows already carry the by-week schedule page as the score source for these two fixtures.

what: The Titans' former domain titansfootball.com is a parked sale page offered by GoDaddy, and https://www.titans.com/team/depth-chart returns HTTP 500.
why_it_matters: A club without a working official depth route would have had no depth rows at all.
what_would_clear_it: CLOSED: the club's live official route is https://www.tennesseetitans.com/team/depth-chart, which publishes a dated unofficial chart. The Titans capture is in data/avail-graph/depth/TEN.txt.

what: The Houston Texans publish their depth chart as a single rendered image with no machine-readable rows. The same image URL was observed on 2026-11-15 by the market desk and again on 2026-11-18 by this session, so the failure is confirmed on two independent dates.
why_it_matters: Texans replacement depth is blank. Transcribing the image by eye would create an inferred depth order with no source text behind it, which the brief forbids.
what_would_clear_it: An authorised structured source for the Texans' depth order, captured with a hash. Until then the rows stay blank and flagged.

what: Earlier in this session six clubs had no official depth capture anywhere in the repository.
why_it_matters: Replacement depth and expected starters were blank for those clubs.
what_would_clear_it: CLOSED: all 32 clubs now have an official depth capture in data/avail-graph/depth/. 31 parse to rows; Houston remains image-only under AG-04.

what: The Chargers' own depth chart (captured 2026-11-18) still prints Daiyan Henley at LB slot 1, although the official NFL roundup of 2026-11-10 records that Denver acquired him from the Chargers.
why_it_matters: A depth chart that still names a departed player will hand the model a starter who cannot play.
what_would_clear_it: The club refreshes the chart; until then the row is flagged AG-21 and excluded from expected-starter use.

what: The Chargers' own depth chart still prints Derwin James Jr. at S slot 1 although the club's transaction page places him on injured reserve.
why_it_matters: Same failure mode: a player who cannot play is printed as a starter.
what_would_clear_it: Club refresh of the chart; the row is flagged AG-21 until then.

what: The Chargers' own depth chart still prints Trey Pipkins III at LT slot 2 although the club's transaction page places him on injured reserve.
why_it_matters: Same failure mode.
what_would_clear_it: Club refresh of the chart; the row is flagged AG-21 until then.

what: The Patriots' own depth chart (captured 2026-11-18) still prints TreVeyon Henderson at RB slot 2 although the official NFL roundup of 2026-11-14 places him on injured reserve.
why_it_matters: Same failure mode; the player is absent from the weekly report because he is on IR, not because he is healthy.
what_would_clear_it: Club refresh of the chart; the row is flagged AG-21 until then.

what: The official Week 11 injury report is not published at read time: https://www.nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/reg11 resolved to the Week 10 report (page title 'Official Latest NFL Injury Report for Players - Week 10 of the 2026 Season').
why_it_matters: Any Week 11 availability view built now is a Week 10 view; it must be labelled as such and cannot be used as a Week 11 designation.
what_would_clear_it: Re-read the reg11 URL once the league publishes it (the request must return a Week 11 title rather than a redirect to reg10). A single official club Week 11 injury report has been published (Texans) and is recorded in availability_events.csv as an event, not as a league-wide report.

what: The hashes published by this desk cover the stored extract of each official page (the depth rows, the report rows, the game-centre fields), not the raw server bytes.
why_it_matters: A byte-level hash of the response body is not available for pages that are rendered; the extract hash still detects any later change to the extracted content.
what_would_clear_it: Capture the raw response body where the endpoint allows it, and publish both hashes.

what: The official game centre prints the Los Angeles Rams as 'LAR'; the official schedule page prints 'LA'; the club's own pages print 'Los Angeles Rams'.
why_it_matters: The same club has three official spellings, which will break naive joins.
what_would_clear_it: Publish the official string verbatim and carry the alias map; a league-wide alias table is the fix.

what: The Patriots-Lions fixture was played in Munich: the official game centre prints Location 'MUNICH' and Stadium 'FC BAYERN MUNICH STADIUM'. An earlier desk note recorded a 'Mexico City 2026' mark on the same fixture.
why_it_matters: A venue taken from a decorative logo is wrong; the official game-centre fields are the source of record.
what_would_clear_it: None needed for the venue itself - the official fields are published; the earlier note is superseded.

what: Six club transaction links (EV-11 to EV-15 and EV-17) were read from a club 'Latest Transactions' block; their publication dates were not read, so the date cell is blank.
why_it_matters: An event without a date cannot be ordered against a capture timestamp, so it can only be flagged, not used as a dated before/after.
what_would_clear_it: Read each transaction page's own date line.

what: Two official statements about Lamar Jackson's absence give 6-9 weeks and 6-10 weeks.
why_it_matters: Collapsing them into one number would be an inference; both are published and the range is kept.
what_would_clear_it: An official club statement with a single number, if the club ever issues one.

what: The official Week 10 report carries rows for the 28 clubs that played; the four clubs on bye (CHI, DEN, PHI, TB) have no rows at all, so 'no row' for them means 'no fixture', not 'no injury'.
why_it_matters: A naive read would treat a missing club as a healthy club.
what_would_clear_it: Read the club's own roster/transactions page for a club with no report row (reserved for a later sweep).

what: The official by-week schedule page prints a weather field for only one Week 10 fixture ('Weather Clearnight' for Chargers-Ravens); no roof or surface field is printed on the official game centre.
why_it_matters: The roof/surface and wind overlay requirement has no official NFL field to read; the venue names are published instead.
what_would_clear_it: A league- or club-published roof designation for the 90-minute window, per venue.

what: In 32 official depth-chart groups every player the club prints in the first slot is designated Out on the official Week 10 report, so the expected starter for that group cannot be read from the chart alone.
why_it_matters: The replacement is published as the next available name in the same official group, with its depth string; without a read Game Book the row cannot be closed.
what_would_clear_it: Read the official Game Book for the fixture, which names the player who actually started.

what: Some official charts print an empty slot in a group (for example the Bears' DL row and the Ravens' DB row).
why_it_matters: An empty slot is a statement by the club that it publishes no further name there; it is preserved as an empty slot rather than closed up with a guess.
what_would_clear_it: None needed; the empty slot is preserved faithfully and marked on the row.

what: In 17 replacement rows the official chart prints no further available name in the group, so the replacement cell is blank.
why_it_matters: A blank replacement is honest; filling it from a roster or from a guess would break the no-inference rule.
what_would_clear_it: An official club announcement naming the replacement, or the Game Book's starting lineup.

what: Eleven availability-graph rows are contradicted by an official club or league transaction event: the player named in the chart is on injured reserve, has been traded, or has been waived.
why_it_matters: A chart row that an official transaction has already invalidated must not feed an expected-starter value.
what_would_clear_it: The club refreshes its chart. Until then the row carries the AG-21 flag and the contradicting official event with its link.

what: The official Week 11 schedule page prints a 'Mexico City 2026' mark beside Vikings-49ers and names no stadium for that fixture or for Bengals-Commanders.
why_it_matters: Two Week 11 venues were blank rather than inferred from the city or from a ticket link.
what_would_clear_it: CLOSED: the official game centre for each fixture was read and its Location and Stadium fields are published: Vikings-49ers prints MEXICO CITY / ESTADIO BANORTE, Bengals-Commanders prints LANDOVER, MD / NORTHWEST STADIUM. The hotel-link stadium names were replaced with those official fields.

what: The official NFL inactive list - the list of players a club deactivates on game day - was published for all 14 Week 10 fixtures, but the desk initially carried only the Game Book link for it.
why_it_matters: The inactive list is an official record of who did not play. Without it an expected starter who was deactivated could still be published as the expected starter; with it, 138 chart rows are excluded against the official list and 43 groups have no available first-slot name.
what_would_clear_it: CLOSED: the official inactive list for all 14 fixtures is captured in data/avail-graph/inactives_week10.csv (158 rows) and joined into the availability graph as the official_inactive_list column. Source: the official nfl.com Week 10 inactives article plus the official Thursday-night and Monday-night inactives articles.

what: The official nfl.com pregame article 'Week 10 injuries to monitor for Sunday's games' names eleven players as officially active or officially inactive, several of whom carry no designation on the weekly report.
why_it_matters: A player removed from the injury report is active but the report alone does not say so; the official pregame article does.
what_would_clear_it: Re-read the pregame article each week and record the named active/inactive statuses. Nine of the eleven are already captured in the inactive list; the two 'active' statements are not yet in a structured file.
